# `item picture` commands

## `item picture clear`

Remove the item's picture: unlinks it and its thumbnail from the item (bytes and history kept); the item then shows its newest remaining image.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Additional resources | attachment: standard |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.picture.clear` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow item picture clear "Pipe Sealant" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Wrong photo" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "item picture clear", "input": {"item": "Pipe Sealant"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | `ITEM` | string | yes | no | — | Item id or full name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 400 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | The item's current version. |
| `keep_file` | `--keep-file` | boolean | no | no | false | Keep the picture linked to the item as an ordinary file. Then, as the newest image, it is still shown. |

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

## `item picture get`

Download an item's picture or thumbnail (verified bytes): a reader of items sees the pictures without the attachment capability, and no other file.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/transfers/item.picture.get` |
| External binary body | output |

### MCP

## `item picture set`

Upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP as the item's picture: linked to the item as a file, then chosen.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Additional resources | attachment: standard |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/transfers/item.picture.set` |
| External binary body | input |

### CLI

`bookflow item picture set "Pipe Sealant" sealant.jpg --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Shelf photo" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "item picture set", "input": {"item": "Pipe Sealant", "original_filename": "sealant.jpg", "media_type": "image/jpeg"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change", "transport": {"input_file": "/permitted-directory/receipt.pdf"}}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `thumbnail_attachment` | `--thumbnail-attachment` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A small copy of the picture already uploaded (at most 1,000,000 bytes), linked to the item if it is not. |
| `item` | `ITEM` | string | yes | no | — | Item id or full name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 400 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | The item's current version. |
| `original_filename` | `--original-filename` | string | yes | no | — | Basename only.; minimum length 1; maximum length 255; Required in JSON/Python; CLI defaults to PATH basename |
| `media_type` | `--media-type` | string | no | no | "application/octet-stream" | Ignored for the stored type: the bytes decide JPEG, PNG or WebP.; maximum length 127; CLI guesses MIME type from PATH unless explicitly supplied |
| `caption` | `--caption` | string | no | no | "Item picture" | Caption on the item's link to the file.; maximum length 2048 |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `PATH` | Required input file on the calling machine. Original filename defaults to its basename; media type defaults to the guessed MIME type, or application/octet-stream. Explicit metadata options override these defaults. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |

| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### External binary body

The registry declares one `input` body separately from the JSON input and output models.

Python: pass a caller-owned binary source as `input_stream=` to `client.run('item picture set', input, ...)` or the named command method. Paths and stream objects are never command JSON fields. The return value is typed JSON metadata.

JSON requires `original_filename`; the CLI supplies its PATH basename when omitted. Python and HTTP default `media_type` to `application/octet-stream`. `--original-filename` and `--media-type` override CLI inference.

See [binary transfers](../transfers.md) for executable file examples, HTTP encoding, limits, dry runs, and local completion verification.

| `picture` | dict \| null | yes | yes | — | What the item now shows (see `item show`). |
| `thumbnail` | dict \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `linked` | array[string] | no | no | [] | Attachment ids newly linked to the item. |
| `unlinked` | array[string] | no | no | [] | Attachment ids unlinked from the item. |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "dry_run": false,
  "full_name": "value",
  "item": "value",
  "linked": [],
  "picture": null,
  "thumbnail": null,
  "unlinked": [],
  "version": 1,
  "warnings": []
}
```

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH` | That idempotency key was used for a different command or input. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_IN_USE` | The record is still used by active records. |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VALUE_RANGE` | The value is outside its allowed range or storage bounds. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
